question.prompt: How many three-digit numbers are divisible by \(13?\)

solutions.explanation:
Every positive number divisible by \(13\) can be written as \(13k\), where \(k\) is a positive integer. Finding the first and last eligible multipliers lets us count all the numbers without listing them.

At the lower end,
\[
13\cdot7=91,\qquad 13\cdot8=104,
\]
so \(8\) is the first multiplier producing a three-digit number. At the upper end,
\[
13\cdot76=988,\qquad 13\cdot77=1001,
\]
so \(76\) is the last.

Every integer multiplier from \(8\) through \(76\) produces a different three-digit multiple, and every three-digit multiple occurs this way. Including both endpoints, the count is
\[
76-8+1=\boxed{69},
\]
choice C.
